newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag targets early break-even for telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Viag targets early break-even for telecoms.

text.p: German diversified utility Viag AG said on Tuesday that its fledgling mobile telephone business could become profitable earlier than it had previously forecast.
"I hope that we will have reached break-even by 2001," Georg Obermeier, Viag's management board chairman, said at a management conference in Munich.
The group had previously forecast break-even in mobile telecommunications by 2002.

Obermeier said that the current group structure, which divides it into five divisions, would remain stable in coming years. He said the holding structure was the best one for managing such a multi-faceted organisation.
Management's tasks included following an active policy of portfolio management and pursuing a policy of buying and selling businesses, which was made easier by the holding structure.
Obermeier said majority ownership of a subsidiary was sufficient for Viag and that 100-percent ownership was not strictly necessary.
Bourse listings for subsidiaries gave them an added boost in the direction of earnings growth.
Viag announced on Monday that it was buying chemicals group Th. Goldschmidt AG as part of its stated aim of strengthening its chemicals division.
